findings.description:
Logical AND (`&&`) used instead of logical OR (`||`) in `isTeamAdminOrOwner` authorization check. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` checks `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` with logical AND instead of logical OR.
WHY: Team owners or team admins will fail the permission check if they do not satisfy both conditions simultaneously, causing an unauthorized `FORBIDDEN` error when attempting to add guests.
HOW: Replace `&&` with `||` so that either a team admin or team owner is granted access.

WHY: When common prefix and suffix characters overlap (e.g. `value = "

Storage.Create failure records legacy duration metrics instead of storage duration metrics. — WHAT: d.recordLegacyDuration is called when d.Storage.Create returns an error.
WHY: Storage failure latency and error counts are recorded against the legacy storage histogram metric instead of the storage histogram metric, corrupting dual-writer observability.
HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration to d.recordStorageDuration.

Delete passes object name instead of resource kind to recordStorageDuration. — WHAT: recordStorageDuration is passed the object instance name instead of options.Kind on successful Storage.Delete.
WHY: Using instance names instead of resource kinds creates high-cardinality Prometheus labels and mismatches the kind label recorded across all other dual writer methods and error branches.
HOW: Pass options.Kind instead of name to d.recordStorageDuration.

Storage.Update failure records legacy duration metrics instead of storage duration metrics. — WHAT: d.recordLegacyDuration is called when d.Storage.Update fails.
WHY: Storage update failures and latencies are recorded against the legacy storage histogram metric instead of the storage histogram metric, distorting telemetry and alerting.
HOW: Change d.recordLegacyDuration to d.recordStorageDuration.

Async Legacy.DeleteCollection records storage duration metric instead of legacy duration metric. — WHAT: d.recordStorageDuration is called inside the async Legacy.DeleteCollection goroutine.
WHY: Asynchronous legacy delete-collection execution time and errors are recorded under the storage duration histogram rather than the legacy duration histogram.
HOW: Change d.recordStorageDuration to d.recordLegacyDuration.

Premature localCache insertion in tagDeviceUI allows rejected devices exceeding the device limit to authenticate on subsequent requests. — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` caches the device ID in `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, without evicting it on error.

WHY: When a new device reaches `TagDevice` after the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and authentication is rejected. However, because `localCache` already recorded the key, the device's next request results in a cache hit in `tagDeviceUI`, which returns `nil` without calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, bypassing the device limit and allowing unauthorized anonymous access.

HOW: In `tagDeviceUI`, only store the key in `localCache` after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` succeeds, or delete the key from `localCache` if `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error.

Cached device key on tagDeviceUI failure allows subsequent requests to bypass AnonymousDeviceLimit — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` stores the device key in `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, but does not evict it when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.
WHY: When a new device is rejected after reaching `AnonymousDeviceLimit`, its device ID remains in `localCache` (29-minute TTL); any subsequent request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns `nil`, and successfully authenticates, completely bypassing the device limit.
HOW: Evict the device cache key on error (e.g. `a.localCache.Delete(taggedDevice.CacheKey())` when `err != nil`) or only store the key in `localCache` after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

Missing `require 'open-uri'` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` causes `open(url)` to fail when opening HTTP/HTTPS URLs. — WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url)` without ensuring `open-uri` is required.
WHY: Without `open-uri` loaded, `Kernel#open` attempts to open `url` as a local filesystem path and raises `Errno::ENOENT` when fetching remote URLs.
HOW: Add `require 'open-uri'` before calling `open(url)` in `import_remote` (or require it at the top of the file).

Unchecked `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on RSS feeds where items only define `description`. — WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called without guarding against `nil` or falling back to `i.description`.
WHY: SimpleRSS items in RSS 2.0 feeds without `<content:encoded>` elements leave `i.content` as `nil`, causing a runtime `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborting feed processing.
HOW: Fall back to `i.description` and ensure content is present before calling `.scrub`.

Duplicate `self.downsize` definition overwrites the 4/5-argument method signature, causing ArgumentError when invoked with separate width and height. — WHAT: Defining `self.downsize` twice in `OptimizedImage` overwrites the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition.
WHY: Ruby does not support method overloading by parameter count or type; the second definition clobbers the first, causing callers like `ResizeEmoji` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) to raise an `ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments)`.
HOW: Unify `self.downsize` into a single method that supports both dimension strings (`"80%"`, `"100x100"`) and separate `max_width`/`max_height` arguments.

Dataclass field default `timezone.now()` is evaluated at module import time instead of instance creation time. — WHAT: `queued` is initialized with a static default expression `timezone.now()`, which evaluates once at class definition / module import time.
WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` created without specifying `queued` will have an identical, stale timestamp recorded at server startup rather than the timestamp when the assignment occurred.
HOW: Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from `dataclasses` to evaluate the timestamp dynamically upon instantiation.

Calling sub! on nil host in before_validation callback causes NoMethodError when validating records with nil host — WHAT: `self.host.sub!` is called without checking if `self.host` is present in the `before_validation` callback.
WHY: When `self.host` is `nil` (e.g. when creating or updating a record without a host value), validation will crash with `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of failing validation gracefully.
HOW: Wrap the normalization in `if self.host.present?` before calling `sub!`.

Prevent `NoMethodError` in `before_validation` when `host` is nil. — WHAT: `self.host.sub!` is called without checking if `self.host` is present in the `before_validation` callback.
WHY: When an `EmbeddableHost` is validated or saved without a `host` attribute, `self.host` is nil and calling `sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of allowing ActiveRecord validations to return an error response.
HOW: Guard the mutation with `if self.host.present?` before modifying `self.host`.

Inverted boolean check causes organization creation to omit the slug when team billing is disabled and assign it prematurely when billing is enabled. — WHAT: The condition for assigning `slug` directly to the new organization was changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.
WHY: When team billing is disabled, the created organization is left with no `slug` (and no `requestedSlug`), while if team billing is enabled, the `slug` is assigned immediately upon creation instead of being held in `metadata.requestedSlug` until billing is completed.
HOW: Restore the negation `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` for the direct `slug` property so that organizations created without billing receive their slug immediately.

Inverted condition sets organization slug when team billing is enabled instead of when it is disabled. — WHAT: The condition for assigning `slug` directly to the new organization was changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

WHY: When team billing is disabled, the organization is created without a `slug`, and when team billing is enabled, both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are set immediately instead of waiting for billing completion.

HOW: Change `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` back to checking `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`.

`totalPages` incorrectly adds an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. — WHAT: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil(...)`.
WHY: When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 users with `limit = 50`), `totalPages` evaluates to 2 instead of 1, causing an extra phantom page to be displayed and allowing navigation to an empty page.
HOW: Use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))`.

Missing re-check of entryPointAssetsCache under write lock causes broken double-checked locking. — WHAT: Missing check for `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`.
WHY: When multiple concurrent requests call `GetWebAssets` on cold start, all waiting goroutines bypass the initial check and redundantly re-read from disk and re-parse the manifest sequentially instead of returning the already cached assets.
HOW: Re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` immediately after acquiring the write lock before executing the manifest loading logic.

Re-check entryPointAssetsCache under write lock to complete double-checked locking pattern — WHAT: Missing check for `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`.
WHY: Multiple concurrent goroutines requesting assets on cold start will pass the initial RLock check and sequentially re-read and parse the manifest, doing redundant I/O and potentially overwriting a valid cache with nil if a later load fails.
HOW: Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` (when not in dev mode) immediately after acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and return the cached value.

AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType for null twice instead of checking rawTokenId. — WHAT: The constructor validates `grantType` twice with `Objects.requireNonNull` instead of validating `rawTokenId` on the fourth check.
WHY: Passing a null `rawTokenId` will not be caught during construction and can result in `NullPointerException` or malformed encoded token IDs later in the lifecycle.
HOW: Change `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

Fix duplicate null-check on grantType instead of rawTokenId in AccessTokenContext constructor — WHAT: `Objects.requireNonNull` checks `grantType` twice instead of validating `rawTokenId` on the second check.
WHY: Passing a `null` `rawTokenId` will bypass constructor validation and fail later when encoding or inspecting the token context.
HOW: Replace the second `grantType` check with `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

Checking response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of !response.ok can cause valid token refresh responses to throw an error. — WHAT: `response.statusText !== "OK"` is used to determine if the Salesforce token refresh request failed.
WHY: `response.statusText` is not guaranteed to be `"OK"` for successful HTTP responses (for example, in HTTP/2 where statusText is empty `""`, or if a proxy alters reason phrases), which causes successful token refresh requests to falsely throw an `HttpError`.
HOW: Check `!response.ok` instead of comparing `response.statusText` against `"OK"`.

Delete condition for retryCount > 1 in scheduleSMSReminders lacks the SMS method filter, deleting non-SMS reminders. — WHAT: The `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition in `deleteMany` is not scoped by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

WHY: Moving `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` into only the first `OR` branch causes `deleteMany` to match and delete any `WorkflowReminder` record across other reminder methods (e.g. WHATSAPP, EMAIL) whenever its `retryCount > 1`.

HOW: Keep `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level of the `where` clause so both `scheduledDate` and `retryCount` conditions only apply to SMS reminders.
